READ-ONLY codebase research at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Do NOT modify any file. Use absolute paths.

Context: backlog-refinement sizing for Jira SFCC-801 "global/country-currency-selector — PWA Component" — a right-anchored slide-in drawer letting shoppers pick shipping country / currency / optionally language, with countries grouped by REGION in collapsible accordion groups, each country row showing a FLAG ICON, country name, and right-aligned CURRENCY CODE.

Investigate and report on these, quoting real code//doc excerpts:

1. /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/config/countries.ts — read it IN FULL. What country data is modelled? How many countries? Does each entry carry a currency? A region? A flag? A locale? Quote the type definition and a couple of representative entries, and state the total count.

2. /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/sites.js — read in full. How many sites, what are their ids, l10n blocks, supported locales, supported currencies, default currency? Summarise as a table. Also check config/default.js for the `siteAliases`/url config that determines URL prefixes.

3. .docs/prd/regional.md — read it and summarise EVERYTHING it says about: the 8 storefronts and 11 locales; the country/currency/region SELECTOR specifically (search for "selector", "country", "currency", "region", "switch"); AU storefront gating; the EU-domestic language choice. Quote verbatim the selector-specific passages.

4. .docs/memory/sprintScope.md and .docs/memory/projectState.md — anything mentioning SFCC-801, SFCC-688, SFCC-817, SFCC-49, SFCC-823, country selector, region selector, locale selector, geolocation. Quote relevant lines. Also note whether these memory docs look current (check dates mentioned).

5. Is there any COUNTRY LIST DATA SOURCE in the repo beyond countries.ts? Search broadly for a country list with currencies — e.g. grep for ISO codes, "AUD", "currencyCode", "countryCode" across overrides/ and config/ and any json/ts data file. Is there a flag-icon asset set anywhere (search overrides/app/assets, overrides/app/static for flag svg/png)? State plainly if flags do not exist.

6. Check whether react-intl / the translations pipeline already provides localized country names (search translations/ and overrides/app/static/translations/ for country name message ids). Also check package.json for any country/flag/i18n data library already installed (e.g. i18n-iso-countries, world-countries, react-world-flags, currency-codes).

7. Does any RADIO atom exist? Search all of overrides/ for a radio component: grep -ri "Radio" on .tsx/.ts. Chakra's Radio/RadioGroup may be used somewhere. Report whether there is a Zimmermann-branded radio atom (zimmRadio or similar) or whether only raw Chakra Radio is used, and where. Same question for an Accordion (grep -ri "Accordion").

Return a concrete, evidence-backed report with absolute file paths and verbatim quotes. Where something does NOT exist, say so explicitly and plainly — that is as important as what does exist.

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- zimmerMANNBuild: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
- zimmerMANNDevImprover: Looks back over completed build work and improves the build chain. Reads the session transcripts and run artefacts for named stories, diagnoses where the loop failed and whose gap it was, checks whether the skills still cite things that are true, and proposes concrete edits to the build skills and loop agents — applied only on Marcel's explicit go.
- zimmerMANNDevOps: Runs deploys, promotions across environments, tags, release cuts and rollbacks on the Zimmermann PWA Kit. Verifies pipeline state live before every action, shows what each environment is running, and executes only on explicit approval. Reports broken gates and stops rather than working around them.
- zimmerMANNPostBuild: The senior dev pass after a build. Audits what zimmerMANNBuild produced against zimmerMANNPreBuild's plan and findings, runs a whole-feature sweep for uniform defects, writes the PR body, and owns the review conversation — pushing and replying only on Marcel's go.
- zimmerMANNPreBuild: The gate and planner before any Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. Gathers and cross-checks every source — Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase and Figma — flags every gap and misalignment, then produces an executable closed-loop build plan and hands off to zimmerMANNBuild. Use at the start of any story, ticket or build task.
- zimmerMANNReview: Reviews someone else's PR as FED Lead. Establishes ground truth, fans out audit angles, verifies every finding before it is raised, then presents for adjudication — Marcel decides the verdict, and comments post only on his go. Loops until the PR is approved.
- zimmerMANNRevImprover: Looks back over completed PR reviews and improves how Marcel reviews. Reads the PR outcome and the review session transcript to judge whether each finding held up, whether anything was missed, and how the review was actually conducted — then proposes concrete edits to zimmerMANNReview, applied only on his explicit go.
- zimmerMANNSprinter: The skill for sprint and agile ceremonies as FED Lead — backlog refinement, sprint planning, standups, retros, and prep for any meeting. Reads Jira and Confluence, drafts what you need to take into the room, and writes to Jira only on your explicit go.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- feature-dev:feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop

- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.

Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.

# Zimmermann - Salesforce PWA Kit (Production)

> **STRICT RULE — TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.**
> Every file created or modified under `overrides/` **must** use `.ts` or `.tsx`.
> `.js` and `.jsx` files are not acceptable here, including theme files, stories, and config modules.
> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`.

Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com, a luxury Australian fashion brand. Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly. See [.docs/architecture.md](.docs/architecture.md) for stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths.

Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).

## Branch Rules

**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.

| Branch                    | Branched from          | Merges to                                                                       | Allowed?      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feature/*`               | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Primary working context for new work                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `fix/*`                   | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `release/*`               | `develop`              | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes        | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
| `hotfix/*`                | `main`                 | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ✅ Yes        | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `develop`                 | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `main`                    | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.

## Hard Rules

1. **Never operate on `develop` or `main`** branches.
2. **Never modify a Tier 1 file** without the developer explicitly naming it in the prompt and confirming owner approval — unless the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) applies. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md).
3. **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — all design token changes go through the UI designer.
4. **Never modify `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, or `worker/main.js`.** These are absolute — the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) does not apply to them, regardless of approver status. `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 CI/CD config and instead follows the standard Hard Rule #2 process (verified-session exception applies).
5. **Never refactor upward.** Fixing a bug in a component does not mean touching the hook or utility it calls.
6. **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
7. **Never add or remove packages** from `package.json` without integration team approval. When approved, always use `npm install` rather than editing `package.json` directly.
8. **Never modify test configuration files** (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `tests/lighthouserc.js`).
9. **Never delete files** without being explicitly asked in the current prompt. You may propose deletion and let a human confirm.
10. **Never touch more than one protection tier** in a single change without stopping to confirm scope with the developer.
11. **Never assume a hook is safe to modify** because it has a simple name — check the frozenFiles list first.
12. **When requirements are unclear, ask one clarifying question at a time.** Do not proceed with assumptions and do not batch questions. Wait for the answer before asking the next question or writing any code.
13. **Never use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`** on `release/**`, `main`, or `develop`. This flag bypasses all edit confirmations and is only permitted in CI automation contexts, never in interactive developer sessions on shared or protected branches.
14. **Never reference code from a later sprint.** Check [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) before scoping any new work. If a task depends on a component, hook, or integration that belongs to a later sprint, stop and ask whether to build a placeholder or whether that sprint is already complete.
15. **Never create a git commit, push to remote, or open/close a PR** without the developer explicitly requesting it in the current prompt. Resuming from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit — wait for an explicit ask.

## Tier 1 Approval — How It's Actually Enforced

Claude Code's confirmation prompt before touching a Tier 1 file (Hard Rule #2) is a workflow
safeguard, not the security boundary — it can't be, since it only governs what Claude itself
does, not what any other tool or a direct `git push` can do. The real enforcement is server-side:

- [CODEOWNERS](../CODEOWNERS) routes every Tier 1 path to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, a
  real GitHub org team.
- Branch protection on `develop`/`main`/`release/**` requires an approving code-owner review
  before merge — this is the actual gate, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
  involvement, so it can't be affected by a broken or delayed CI run.
- `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`'s `tier1-guard` job posts a loud warning and an
  owner-contact-map on any PR touching a Tier 1 path. It is **not** a required status check —
  GitHub locked down cross-run check-run updates in Feb 2025, which made a "hard-fail until
  approved, then flip to pass on review" required check impossible to implement reliably (a
  fresh commit is needed to re-evaluate it, since a later review can't flip an earlier run's
  result). The CODEOWNERS-based review requirement above is the real, working block.

Because the actual gate lives in GitHub, not in Claude's judgement, this file does not encode
personal names or email addresses as a bypass condition — a string in a shared, version-controlled
file is not an identity check; anyone (or any other Claude session) could satisfy it by typing it.
Instead, Claude may verify the real, authenticated identity behind the current session:

- Before pausing to ask for Tier 1 confirmation, run `gh api user --jq .login`, then check
  `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members --jq '.[].login'` (or check for `admin`
  via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/collaborators/<login>/permission`). If that GitHub
  login is a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or holds repo admin, Claude may proceed
  with the edit after stating which Tier 1 file is being touched and why — no separate
  confirmation message is required, since GitHub already recognises that account as an approver.
- If the authenticated login is **not** a member/admin, Claude must still stop per Hard Rule #2:
  name the file, and require the developer to secure an approving review from
  `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` before the PR can merge. CODEOWNERS auto-requests that review
  and branch protection blocks the merge without it, regardless of what `tier1-guard` reports.
- This check only ever reduces _how many times Claude pauses to ask_. It changes nothing about
  what GitHub will actually allow to merge — that's deliberate, so a compromised or careless
  Claude session can't grant itself write access to a frozen file.

## Coding Task Workflow

Every coding task follows these four steps in order. Do not skip ahead — pause at the marked points and wait for the user.

1. **Clarify requirements.** Identify every gap, ambiguity, or contradiction in the request and the relevant `.docs/`. Confirm each one with the user before moving on — no assumptions. See Hard Rule #12: ask one question at a time.
2. **Plan.** State the files you intend to touch, _why_ each one is being touched, and any base template files that will need to be copied to `overrides/`. Then **pause** and wait for the user to confirm the plan. See the **Minimal changes** rule below.
3. **Copy first (if any).** For every base template file identified in step 2, follow the **Copy-first rule** in the Rules section. Then **pause** and let the user test and stage the override files before any functional changes.
4. **Implement.** Make the planned modifications. Remove the `console.log` markers from step 3 once the user confirms the overrides are rendering. Before committing a non-trivial code change, run a local CodeRabbit review: confirm the CLI is installed and authenticated (`coderabbit auth status`; if not authenticated, `coderabbit auth login --api-key "$CODERABBIT_API_KEY"` — see `.env.sample`), then `cr review --light --base develop` (use `main` instead on a `release/**`/`hotfix/**` branch). **The CLI is required, not optional** — if it isn't installed or authenticated, stop and have the developer install it (https://www.coderabbit.ai/cli) and run `npm run env -- init` to pull the shared key, rather than committing without a local review. The review itself is still advisory relative to the actual merge gate (the GitHub PR review remains the real gate) — use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth fixing before the commit vs. leaving it for the PR review to catch, but the review must actually run.

**Responding to a CodeRabbit PR review.** Once CodeRabbit finishes reviewing an open PR, always leave an explicit in-thread reply for every finding, whether it's fixed or not — CodeRabbit's learning feature picks up patterns from PR conversation, so silence teaches it nothing and an explanation teaches it to stop flagging the same non-issue. A fix commit alone, with no reply posted on the thread, doesn't count. For a finding that gets fixed, a short in-thread reply confirming the fix (referencing the commit is fine) is enough. For a finding that is *not* being fixed because it conflicts with this repo's own rules/docs/architecture (e.g. a Tier 1 exception that was actually followed correctly, an intentional design tradeoff already recorded in `.docs/`) — reply in-thread explaining the specific rule or doc that justifies not changing it, so CodeRabbit's learning has the context to recognise the same pattern next time instead of re-flagging it. Never silently dismiss a finding without a reply.

## Multi-site & Routing

The SFCC sites are hard routing and config boundaries — **never bleed config across sites.** Never assume a storefront's routing, URL prefix, checkout ownership, or consent defaults without checking [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md).

## Commands

- `npm start` — local dev at http://localhost:3000. **Do not run!** Ask the user to restart if needed.
- `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run push` (Managed Runtime deploy)

## Accessibility

Target WCAG 2.2 AA. Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible — document why.

## Rules

*Day-to-day code-writing conventions live in `.claude/rules/` and load automatically:
[conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) (cross-cutting: naming, imports, DRY, security),
[typescript.md](.claude/rules/typescript.md) (TS idioms), [css.md](.claude/rules/css.md)
(Chakra tokens, `.scss`), and [components.md](.claude/rules/components.md)
(component/hook/utility structure, Storybook categorisation, composition). The rules below
are project-specific behaviours and security guardrails that don't fit there.*

- **No mocking:** All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths.
- **Environment variables:** Never hardcode secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials anywhere in the codebase. Local values live in `.env.shared` (tier-independent) and `.env.<tier>` (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod) — gitignored, managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`; full command reference in `.env.sample`'s header) — and are set as platform environment variables on Managed Runtime for staging/prod. When adding a new env var: (1) add it to `.env.sample` tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on its own comment line above the key (value only if it's a non-secret public identifier, otherwise leave blank — never a trailing comment, or a blank placeholder reads as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard), (2) run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold the new key into `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>`, then fill in the real value locally. Never put tokens, bearer credentials, DSNs, or licence keys in `.env.sample`. Non-personal shared/tier values may additionally be centrally published via `npm run env -- push <scope>` (tier-1-approvers only) to this repo's GitHub Environments — genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal`, e.g. your own Atlassian or Contentful CMA token) must never be pushed.
- **Comments:** Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments (except when removing the corresponding code) — leave for the user to delete manually. (For _new_ comments introduced in a PR, see conventions.md.)
- **Icons:** Use `overrides/app/components/icons` — this is the single source of truth for all icons (Zimmermann custom and base PWA). Do not import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly. If a required icon is missing from the overrides set, ask the user — do not substitute a visually different one.
- **Styling:** Chakra UI component props first; use a `.scss` file alongside the component only when Chakra props are insufficient. The `overrides/app/theme/` folder is the source of truth — brand tokens in `foundation/` (Tier 1), one file per component override in `components/` (Tier 2), composed in `index.ts`. Register a new component override in `theme/components/index.ts`.
- **Minimal changes:** Make the smallest change that fully achieves the task. Do not remove or replace existing base template functionality unless explicitly instructed. When a larger change (e.g., a refactor for cleanliness) seems beneficial, propose it and wait for user confirmation — never do it silently.
- **Copy-first rule:** For any task that requires overriding base template files that do not yet exist in `overrides/`, the very first step is to prepare all of them at once: (1) copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`, (2) convert each to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`) and update relevant imports, (3) run `npx tsc --noEmit`, (4) add a temporary `console.log` to each copied file identifying it (e.g. `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')`) so the user can verify the override is rendering instead of the base component, then **stop and present the converted files to the user to test**. Wait for the user to confirm the overrides are rendering before making any functional changes; remove the `console.log` statements once confirmed. Never skip this step or bundle it silently with functional changes.

## Consent & Marketing

- **Didomi:** Do not load any third-party script until Didomi consent is granted. Gate all analytics, marketing, and tracking scripts behind Didomi callbacks.
- **Marketing opt-in:** Unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked). Sync opt-in state: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys.

_Per-storefront Didomi defaults, GTM/Enhanced Conversions setup, and Inside Chat rules: see [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md)._

## Type Definitions

- **Component-specific prop types:** co-locate at the top of the component file.
- **Shared types** (Commerce Cloud entities, API responses, shared hook signatures): `overrides/app/types/` — split into `commerce.ts`, `components.ts`, `hooks.ts`, re-exported via `index.ts`.
- Don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly.

## Testing

Three layers: **Vitest** (unit logic) · **Storybook** `play` (component interactions) · **Playwright** (E2E). Write tests only where failure would be non-obvious or costly to debug — data mapping, integration boundaries, complex state, and pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken. Every UI component needs a `.stories.tsx`; every logic-heavy feature needs a `.test.ts` or a story `play`.

Full layer guidance, file layout, selector priority, and mocking policy: [.claude/rules/testing.md](.claude/rules/testing.md). (The no-MSW rule in Rules applies to production paths only.)

## Graceful Degradation

Each external system must fail independently — one outage must not break the whole page. Two defaults override any per-system behaviour: **fail closed on consent** (if consent state is unknown, load no third-party scripts), and **never silently substitute a different checkout, payment, or commerce flow** when an integration is down — surface an explicit error instead.

## Performance

Mobile page speed is a top priority. Every change that touches rendering, data fetching, or assets must not regress it.

- **LCP budget is tight (≤ 2s at p75 mobile)** — Defer every third-party script that isn't required for first paint. Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM, Optimizely, Inside Chat, Narvar EDD, reCAPTCHA, etc.) must not block LCP — use `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection. If a new third-party integration looks like it might land on the critical path, flag it before merging.
- **Images:** Always use lazy loading and serve correctly sized images. Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting:** Prefer dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on initial render.
- **Data fetching:** Avoid over-fetching — request only the fields you need. Waterfall requests are not acceptable; parallelise where possible.
- **Bundle size:** Do not introduce large dependencies without confirming with the user.
- **Dependencies:** Before implementing any feature that may require a third-party library, check `package.json` for what is already installed. Evaluate whether an existing dependency can satisfy the requirement. If a better third-party option exists, present the recommendation (existing vs. new, with trade-offs) and wait for user approval before installing anything.

## Gotchas

- **`<img src>` does not work for a project-owned SVG.** `pwa-kit-dev`'s webpack config applies
  `svg-sprite-loader` (server target) / `ignore-loader` (client target) to every `.svg` import
  with an unscoped `test: /\.svg$/` — not limited to `node_modules`, so a brand-new file under
  `overrides/app/assets/svg/` is affected exactly as much as a base-package icon. Neither loader
  produces a URL an `<img src>` can consume. Commit the SVG to `overrides/app/assets/svg/` as
  the source-of-truth reference, then inline its `<path>` data verbatim as JSX inside a
  `chakra.svg` instead — copy the real path data exactly, never hand-redraw it. `ZimmLogo`
  (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmLogo/index.tsx`) is the established reference
  implementation. Vitest and Storybook both have their own separate SVG handling that makes
  `<img src>` appear to work in tests/stories — this only breaks in the real app build, so it
  will not be caught by a green test suite.
- **Theme runtime errors:** Custom components (e.g. `ListMenu`) must be defined in the theme object or destructuring will throw.
- **Commerce SDK types not importable:** Check `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` for generated definitions, or declare a narrow local `type`.
- **Magento password migration:** Passwords were not migrated from Magento — all existing customers must reset at go-live. Do not assume any saved credentials exist. Account creation and login flows must handle this gracefully (CFD-013).

# Styling an Override Component

How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
companion.

---

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
   type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
which is what `audit:tokens` is for.

## Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
  comment for traceability.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy

`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
if only one of them is ever typed.

`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component

If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import, which is correct for that file).

The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
override and isn't.

**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.

An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.

## Component-local tokens

When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.

See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)

**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.

When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.

## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)

If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies. When one of them does get
overridden, keep its default export API-compatible and put brand styling in a theme
recipe rather than a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't require a second
export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

**As of `7b9b5dc`, none of the three is overridden at all** — no component override, no
theme recipe, nothing registered for them in `theme/components/index.ts`. Verify current
state before relying on any of this. `protectedFiles.md` and `CODEOWNERS` list those
paths forward-lookingly, not descriptively. An earlier revision of this paragraph cited
`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` as holding their styling; neither
file has ever existed on any branch.

---

## Co-locating a component's theme file

A component's recipe may live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, or an organism's own
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/<name>/<name>.css.ts`) instead of in
`theme/components/`. Either way it's still registered in
`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key
passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an
organisational choice with no runtime difference.

**Governance follows the file, not the folder.** `theme/components/` is Tier 2, gated to
the UI designer (protectedFiles.md). A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is deliberately routed
differently: CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule sends it to the
owning squad(s) only, dropping the Tier 1/2 approver requirement that the surrounding
directory (e.g. `header/`, `footer/`) otherwise carries. That's intentional — a co-located
file is for composing a component's own layout from **already-established** tokens
(spacing, colour, typography scale), not for authoring new raw design values. Authoring an
actual new token still means editing `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a `theme/components/`
recipe that's still designer-owned (`header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts` — the
files that remain in that directory) — both stay behind the full gate.

# CSS & Styling Conventions

Chakra UI and `.scss` conventions. See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Rules > Styling for the
higher-level policy (Chakra props first, `.scss` only when insufficient, theme file
ownership/tiers) — this file covers the concrete day-to-day rules underneath that policy.

---

## Tokens — no hardcoded design values

Chakra UI props must use the Chakra token system — no hardcoded hex colours, no pixel
values for spacing, no raw font sizes. Tokens belong in
[overrides/app/theme/foundation/](../../overrides/app/theme/) (Tier 1 — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)).

```tsx
// ❌ hardcoded
<Box color="#1A1A1A" padding="16px" />

// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string — resolves correctly (theme.colors/theme.space ARE
// registered from the Zimmermann foundations) but is still not allowed in an override
// component; see overrideStyling.md's hierarchy point 2 for why
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ token, as a raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

Type is its own case, not shown above — set it with `textStyle` (`textStyle="body2"`), never
a raw `fontSize`, per [overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md) point 1. There's no
`var(--zimm-*)` substitute for the composite `textStyle` expansion itself, only for its
individual pieces (`var(--zimm-font-size-*)` etc.), so `textStyle` stays a bare key —
it's the one entry in the hierarchy that isn't a colour/spacing token.

**The raw-hex/px/rem/em half of this has a script but no CI gate yet.**
`npm run audit:tokens` (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) scans `overrides/app/components/**`
and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` for exactly this — see
[overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md)'s `Never` note for the full scope and its
acknowledged-exception rules. It's not wired into CI (no `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` rule
either), so nothing blocks a merge that skips running it — that's still a real gap, just not
an unstarted one.
The bare-token-vs-`var(--zimm-*)` half above **is** mechanically enforced for recipe files —
see `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`, which runs on every `npm run test` — though it
can't see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop; that half still relies on review.

---

## `.scss` — only when Chakra props are insufficient

Per AGENTS.md, reach for a `.scss` file alongside a component only when Chakra's prop system
genuinely can't express what's needed (e.g. complex pseudo-selectors, keyframe animations,
print styles). When you do:

- **File naming:** matches the component file exactly — `productTile.scss` next to
  `productTile/index.tsx` (see [conventions.md](./conventions.md) > File naming and folder
  structure for the folder layout this sits in).
- **Scoped, co-located only.** No global stylesheets outside `overrides/app/theme/` — a
  component's `.scss` file must only affect that component's own markup.
- **Nesting depth ≤ 3 levels.** Beyond that, the selector is almost always reaching into a
  child component's internals rather than styling its own root — a sign the styling belongs
  in that child instead, or that Chakra's `sx` prop / a theme variant would express it more
  directly.
- **No ID selectors.** Class-based only — an ID selector's specificity makes it
  disproportionately hard to override later (including by a legitimate future Chakra
  variant), and IDs aren't guaranteed unique when a component renders more than once on a
  page.
- **No `!important`** without an inline comment explaining why the override is genuinely
  unavoidable (e.g. fighting a third-party widget's inline styles) — same reasoning as the
  `any`/non-null-assertion escape hatches in [typescript.md](./typescript.md): allowed, but
  the reason has to be visible at the point of use, not left for the next reader to guess.
- **Prefer Chakra's `sx` prop or a theme variant extension over a new `.scss` file** for
  anything that's really just "a Chakra style the prop system doesn't have a named prop for"
  — a new global class is a bigger footprint than a one-off `sx` override, and `sx` keeps the
  style co-located with the JSX that uses it instead of a separate file to keep in sync.

## General — every file in a PR

These apply to all `.ts`/`.tsx` files Claude creates or modifies, regardless of folder.

- **TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.** `.js`/`.jsx` is not acceptable here — see AGENTS.md.
- **No commented-out code blocks introduced by this PR** unless accompanied by an explicit
  strong reason in a comment immediately above. Existing comments are preserved per AGENTS.md —
  the rule is about _introducing_ new dead code, not removing old.
- **No `console.log` or `console.error` calls** outside of error boundaries or explicit
  developer-tooling files. Use the project's logger when one is introduced.
- **No hardcoded design values** — Chakra token usage is a whole topic of its own now; see
  [css.md](./css.md).
- **React rules of hooks apply everywhere hooks are called.** Only call hooks at the top
  level of a component or another hook. No conditional, looped, or nested hook calls.
- **TypeScript idioms** (`any`, `type` vs `interface`, and the rest) — see
  [typescript.md](./typescript.md).
- **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored identifiers and copy (`colour`, `centre`,
  `organisation`). Override files keep upstream Salesforce spelling verbatim.
- **Apply DRY, KISS, and SOLID.** Don't repeat logic — extract to a shared utility or hook
  once the same pattern appears in two places. Prefer the simplest design that works; resist
  speculative abstractions. Keep modules to a single responsibility; split a file when it
  starts mixing concerns.
- **No magic numbers or strings.** Any literal value with semantic meaning — pixel
  thresholds, retry counts, country codes, feature flag names, status strings, error
  codes — must be a named constant (`const MAX_RETRIES = 3`) or live in a config/enum
  module. Excepted: `0`, `1`, `-1` in obvious idiomatic uses, and string literals that _are_
  the value (e.g. CSS class names, JSX text).
- **Payment credentials — never logged, never persisted client-side.** Gift card numbers,
  gift card PINs, credit card PANs, CVVs and similar secrets must not appear in any
  `console.*` call, Sentry breadcrumb / event, GTM dataLayer push, analytics event, MRT
  access log, or response body returned to the browser beyond a masked form. Never store
  them in `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookies — form state lives in
  React only and is cleared on unmount. Submit them in the POST **body**, never as a
  query string (URLs end up in MRT access logs, browser history, Referer headers). After
  submit, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). Do not add body-logging
  middleware on routes that carry these fields. Logger and Sentry `beforeSend` must
  redact them. See [.docs/prd/giftcards.md §10](../../.docs/prd/giftcards.md) for the
  GiveX-specific rationale (only the card's serial portion may be displayed or logged).
- **`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must always wrap its value in a sanitizer call**
  (e.g. `DOMPurify.sanitize(...)`) — never pass raw/unsanitized HTML (CMS content,
  API responses, user input). Unsanitized HTML injection is an XSS vector. Enforced
  by a `semgrep.yml` rule at PR review time — get it right at authoring time instead
  of finding out post-review.

---

## File naming and folder structure

- **Zimmermann-authored files and folders:** `camelCase` (e.g. `productTile.tsx`,
  `useWishlist.ts`, `formatPrice.ts`).
- **Override files (mirroring a base Salesforce file):** keep the original kebab-case
  filename and folder name exactly (e.g. `product-tile.tsx`). This makes the origin of a
  file obvious at a glance.
- **Component folder layout:** each component lives in its own folder under
  [overrides/app/components/](../../overrides/app/components/). Use `index.tsx` for the
  component itself so imports stay clean:

  ```
  overrides/app/components/productTile/
    index.tsx              ← the component
    index.stories.tsx      ← Storybook story
    index.test.ts          ← Vitest (only if logic-heavy)
    types.ts               ← only if props/types are shared with sibling files
    productTile.scss       ← only if Chakra props are insufficient
  ```

  Import as `import ProductTile from '.../components/productTile'`.

---

## Utilities

- **Pure functions** — no side effects unless clearly intentional and called out in a comment.
- **No imports from `overrides/app/hooks/`** — utilities must not depend on hooks
  (it's the other direction).
- **Vitest required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports or
  one-liners don't need a test.

---

## Imports

- **No circular imports** — if file A imports from file B, B must not import from A
  (check one level deep).
- **No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels** — flag for path-alias review.
- **No imports from internal `node_modules/@salesforce/...` source paths** — use the
  package's published entrypoints (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`).
- **No imports from a later-sprint feature** — cross-check
  `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`.

# Components, Hooks & Storybook Everything about designing, structuring, and presenting a React component or hook in this project. Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS conventions live in [css.md](./css.md). --- ## Components - **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`). No default exports of anonymous functions. - **Props type name** matches the component name: `ProductTileProps` for `ProductTile`, `TopNavProps` for `TopNav`. - **Props type placement:** - _Default:_ declare the `Props` type at the top of the component file. - _Move to `types.ts` in the same folder_ only when (a) the type is consumed by sibling files (story, test, sub-components) **or** (b) it exceeds ~30 lines and mixes with other shared types worth co-locating. - The trigger is _shared consumption_, not line count alone. - **JSDoc** is required on: - Any component used by ≥2 callers (shared components — typically Tier 2 in [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)). - Any exported hook. - Any utility function with non-obvious behaviour. Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient. - **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`). - **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions for "I forgot to mark it optional." - **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get these right at authoring time:** - Every `` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images). - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to announce. - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`, `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role` attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour). --- ## Composition — writing a "clean" component Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline state belongs in a custom hook instead. - **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced** — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not something the build will fail on yet. If this keeps being a problem in practice, adding those two ESLint rules is a cheap follow-up (they're built into ESLint core, no new dependency needed). - **Container/presentational separation.** Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or any `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container component, which then passes the result down. This generalizes the existing "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it). **Exception — Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks** (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including presentational leaves. Both read from a Provider mounted above the route tree, not from a per-page/per-component fetch — so calling one from a leaf doesn't create the SSR/Storybook/parent-composition problem the rule above exists to prevent, and doesn't multiply fetches the way an SDK hook would. `useUiCopy` (`overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts`, Provider at `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/`) is the reference example — `BottomBar` and `ZimmSubscribeSection` both call it directly for microcopy while still receiving their actual business data as props. This exception is narrow: it covers content that is identical for every consumer regardless of route/context, not anything that varies per page. **Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests and stories.** `useUiCopy` degrades to fallback text — `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY` — so a leaf calling it renders with zero setup. `useIntl` **throws** (`react-intl`'s `invariantIntlContext`: _"Could not find required `intl` object"_), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the **base SFCC `_app`**, not by `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. `.storybook/preview.tsx` supplies one for stories precisely because of this; any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer must wrap it too. An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed both hooks degrade gracefully and that both Providers sit in `_app-config`; neither is true of `useIntl`. - **Extract-to-hook threshold.** Pull inline component logic out into a custom hook (`overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`) when either is true: - The component has ≥2 pieces of related `useState` that change together (a strong signal the state belongs in one place, whether that's a custom hook or a single reducer). - Any `useEffect` has a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function — non-trivial meaning more than a single obvious dependency, or the effect does anything beyond a one-line side effect. This one is judgment-heavy, not a hard mechanical gate — `/code-quality` should flag it as a should-fix, not a must-fix, and a component with ≥4 `useState` calls is a reasonable coarse trigger to at least stop and ask "should this be a hook?" --- ## Hooks - **File extension** is `.ts` (no JSX in a hook file). - **Exported function name** matches the filename: `useWishlist.ts` exports `useWishlist`. - **Parameters and return value are typed** — no implicit `any`, no missing return type. See [typescript.md](./typescript.md) for the general typing rules this extends. - **JSDoc** is required on every exported hook, including a `@returns` description. --- ## Storybook Storybook is the canonical place to view components in isolation. Keep it browsable — a flat 200-story sidebar is unusable. ### When a story is required - **Required** for any component exported from its folder under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` (i.e. anything another file imports). - **Not required** for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent (e.g. `productTile/priceRow.tsx` used only by `productTile/index.tsx`). Cover their variants via the parent's stories. - Pages get a story showing the full assembly with representative props — not a story per sub-section. ### Categorisation Story `title` drives the sidebar tree. Pick the first matching category: | Category | What goes here | | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons, Shadows | | `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — both display (Badge, Tag, Link, Avatar, Skeleton) and interactive controls (Button, Input, Checkbox, Select). Tiebreaker: _can it be used outside a form?_ → `Elements/`. | | `Layout/` | Global chrome, navigation, and structural components — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, ListMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination, Seo | | `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared components — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup | | `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, CheckoutContactForm, NewsletterSignup | | `Pages/` | Full page assemblies — PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout, Account | | `Contentful/` | CMS-driven components — HeroBanner, RichText, ContentBlock. Use mock Contentful data in stories so variants are visible without a live CMS connection. | Naming convention: singular for a concept or proper noun (`Foundation`, `Commerce`, `Layout`, `Contentful`); plural for a collection (`Elements`, `Forms`, `Pages`). Examples: ```ts export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Layout/Header' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Elements/Button' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Pages/PDP' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ — eCommerce specific, use Commerce/ export default { title: 'Primitives/Button' }; // ❌ — use Elements/ ``` When in doubt: ask "what does this component _know_ about?" Commerce → `Commerce/`, CMS-driven → `Contentful/`, nothing domain-specific → `Elements/`, page-level composition → `Pages/`. ### Story content - Every story file has a `Default` named export. - Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`) — not for every possible prop combination. - `play` functions only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting; otherwise the story is purely visual.

# Tagging & Environment Promotion

How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.

---

## Tag taxonomy

Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. The **tag-promoted** tiers
(`test` / `uat` / `staging` / `prod`) deploy a specific tag — never "whatever's on a branch right
now." (The continuous tiers are the exception: `dev` and `sit` deploy commit refs, and Test also
takes a branch ref for on-demand quick looks — see the Environment model below.)

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |

**Versioning:**
- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — it counts
  candidate builds, not deployments. The same `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be deployed (and re-deployed) to
  Test on demand; which environment ran which candidate is tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions
  run history, not the tag name.
- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
  relies on.

Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.

---

## Cutting a tag

Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.

**Release candidate (any developer):**

```bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull --ff-only   # fail rather than tag a local merge commit
git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
```

- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.

**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
`main`, then promote it up through `uat` → `staging` → `prod`. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
at this point to produce the GitHub Release.

**Rollback.** The downgrade guard (see below) deliberately blocks deploying an older tag, so a
rollback takes one of two authorised paths:

- **Emergency (fastest) — re-activate the previous bundle in Managed Runtime**, outside the deploy
  pipeline (the rollback procedure in the Environment Topology doc). This does not run the guard, so
  afterwards re-record the baseline so it doesn't treat a superseded tag as live:
  `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record prod v0.1.0`.
- **Controlled — pipeline rollback with the guard override.** Redeploy the known-good tag with
  `rollback=true`; the guard's downgrade check is skipped (the run logs the skip for audit) and
  `record` still runs, so the rolled-back tag becomes the new live baseline:
  `gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.1.0 -f rollback=true`. Because this bypasses the guard,
  its only human gate is the environment's **required reviewers** — so `prod` (and `staging`/`uat`)
  must have required reviewers with "prevent self-review" configured. **Prerequisite: until that is
  set, `rollback=true` is not gated.**

---

## Enforcement — what actually holds the line

On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
order of reliability:

1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.

GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.

---

## Environment model — two categories

| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |

**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.

**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).

---

## Downgrade protection (version-guard)

[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
`deploy-*.yml` workflows:

- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
  we record it ourselves and read it back).
- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
  two-category model above).
- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

---

## The Test gate

`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.

- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB). Bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, and mobile
  page-speed is a top project priority, so bloat is caught at the earliest deployed tier.
- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.

This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.
