tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_resize
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab to test responsive layouts. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>

assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"

<function call omitted for brevity>

See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.\nDaisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"\nAssistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example>\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.\nDaisy: "Please review PR #1234"\nAssistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example>\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.\nDaisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"\nAssistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example> (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)
- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)
- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.
</system-reminder>

# PRD – Regional Storefronts, Consent & Routing

_Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Regional Storefronts", "Country to Storefront Mapping", and "Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL". Last updated: 2026-06-19. SFCC site IDs and locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 BM (2026-06-13)._

---

## 1. Storefronts & URL Prefixes (REG-001 – REG-008, REG-043, DMU-013, DMU-016)

**8 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions in Business Manager:** AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME. A MX domestic site is planned for 2027. EU domestic and EU international remain **separate sites** (REG-006).

> **Status (2026-07-10):** REG-005 is **updated** — the US is now **two separate SFCC sites**: a US domestic site (`/us/`, SFCC checkout only) and a US international site (`/en-ca/`, Global-e checkout only). This supersedes the 2026-06-11 single-site decision. Rationale: managing Global-e complexity is simpler with a dedicated site boundary; inventory pooling and reporting can be handled at the SFCC realm level. **New site IDs require confirmation in Business Manager** — `ZimmermannUSIntl` is the working name for the international site.

Each storefront has its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods, configured independently (REG-002).

11 active locales across the 8 sites (REG-043). EU domestic and EU international remain separate storefronts (REG-006). US domestic and US international are now separate storefronts (REG-005, updated 2026-07-10).

SFCC site IDs and BM locale IDs (verified 2026-06-13):

| Locale           | SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                     | URL prefix                     | Local currency         | Checkout owner          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------- |
| AU (+ Oceania)   | `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                             | `/` (root; x-default hreflang) | AUD                    | SFCC (REG-003)          |
| UK               | `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                          | `/uk/`                         | GBP                    | SFCC (REG-004)          |
| US domestic      | `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                          | `/us/`                         | USD                    | SFCC (REG-005)          |
| US international | `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(confirm locale in BM)_ | `/en-ca/`                      | USD                    | Global-e (REG-005)      |
| EU domestic (EN) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB`                          | `/en-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC (REG-006 dom)      |
| EU domestic (FR) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `fr`                             | `/fr-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU domestic (IT) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `it`                             | `/it-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU domestic (ES) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `es`                             | `/es-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU international | `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                          | `/en-ch/`                      | EUR                    | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
| HK               | `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                          | `/hk/`                         | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-007)      |
| ME               | `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                          | `/en-ae/`                      | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-008)      |

ROW also routed via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` prefixes (DMU-013; see [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md) for full URL strategy). AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — the AU root remains globally crawlable because search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the human geo-redirect; see REG-009 in Section 4).

URL formats: product `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` (the `.html` suffix is **preserved** to maintain existing indexed URLs — DMU-015); category `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no `.html`). Category URLs are updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`) with 301 redirects from all legacy paths (DMU-014).

Business users can manage storefront configuration in SFCC BM at both global and individual storefront levels (REG-010).

The US storefront supports all required US address formats; APO, FPO, and PO Box addresses are **not** supported (REG-012).

### Country → Storefront routing (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet)

The full per-country mapping lives in the source sheet; the FE only needs the routing logic:

- **AU (root):** Australia (default) and all Oceania — American Samoa, Cook Islands, Fiji, Guam, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Northern Marianas, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu. NZ and New Caledonia get Avalara duty/tax; other Oceania destinations are DDU (REG-003).
- **UK (`/uk/`):** United Kingdom only.
- **US (`/us/` domestic):** United States (default) and **Puerto Rico**.
- **US (`/en-ca/` international, Global-e):** Canada, Mexico, and all other Americas — Caribbean, Central America, and South America (Argentina, Aruba, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, Bolivia, Brazil, BVI, Cayman, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Grenada, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad & Tobago, Turks & Caicos, USVI, Uruguay, Venezuela, etc.).
- **EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`):** France (default), Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Ireland, Portugal, Greece, **Denmark**, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino.
- **EU international (`/en-ch/`, Global-e):** Non-EU Europe (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Gibraltar, Greenland, Faroe Islands, Channel Islands, etc.) and **all of Africa** (Algeria, Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cape Verde, Chad, Comoros, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Réunion, São Tomé, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Also includes Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname.
- **HK (`/hk/`, Global-e):** Hong Kong (default), China, Macau, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Maldives, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Timor-Leste, Uzbekistan. **Also includes "Australia" as a destination** — this is the REG-027 path for non-Oceania clients who select AU in the country selector (they are routed to HK, not the gated AU site).
- **ME (`/en-ae/`, Global-e):** UAE (default), Bahrain, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia.

**Denmark routing is resolved → EU Domestic** (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet confirms; remove from Open Items).

> Geographic anomalies (mapping sheet): Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname all route to **EU International** despite being in the Americas/African geography. This follows fulfilment territory, not landmass — flagged for awareness; routing tables must follow the sheet verbatim.

---

## 2. Entry Routing & Mismatch Detection (REG-009, REG-013 – REG-035)

- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
- **AU is gated** to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IPs only (REG-009). AU is the `x-default` hreflang and must remain crawlable, so it is never blocked at the network level. A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. Image/News, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, AppleBot, YandexBot, Baiduspider, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, Discordbot). Fail open: if UA looks botty but isn't matched, skip the redirect rather than apply it — false-positive cost is zero, missing a real crawler hurts SEO.
- All other storefronts use **mismatch detection** (REG-014): a country slide-out is shown on the first visit if the user's IP country does not match the storefront's shipping region (REG-015). Two CTAs: redirect to the appropriate storefront, or open the country selector (REG-016). A warning is shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-017). Not shown if country matches (REG-018). Shown on first visit only — does not reappear after selection or dismissal (REG-019).
- **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU (REG-020, REG-025). Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field (REG-021). Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, all other storefronts English only (REG-023). Selected EU locale reflected in URL (REG-024).
- AU is gated and does **not** allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites (REG-025).
- **China** selected from any country selector routes to HK (REG-026).
- **Australia** selected from another storefront's country selector (i.e. clients outside Oceania) routes to HK (REG-027).
- Global-e checkout locks the shipping country — determined by country selector pre-checkout, cannot be changed inside Global-e (REG-028).

### EU language mismatch (REG-029 – REG-035)

When a user's GEO-IP country doesn't match the URL language on the EU domestic storefront, show a language mismatch modal in the current URL language (REG-029, REG-031). Two CTAs: continue in current language, or switch (REG-032). Country-to-language mapping (REG-030):

- France / Monaco → French (`/fr-eu/`)
- Italy / San Marino → Italian (`/it-eu/`)
- Spain → Spanish (`/es-eu/`)

Modal does not show when detected country matches the current URL language (REG-033), and is not shown for countries with no dedicated EU locale — they default to `/en-eu/` (REG-034). Logic applies regardless of entry point (Instagram, Google Shopping, direct URL, organic search) (REG-035).

---

## 3. Checkout Ownership

- **SFCC** owns domestic checkout for AU (REG-003), UK (REG-004), US domestic (REG-005), EU domestic (REG-006 dom).
- **Global-e** owns checkout for HK (REG-007), ME (REG-008), US international (REG-005 — now a separate SFCC site), EU international (REG-006 intl) — and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market.
- **AU serves Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands) domestically** via SFCC — not via Global-e. Avalara calculates duties/tax for NZ and New Caledonia specifically (REG-003); other Oceania destinations are DDU.
- Branch checkout ownership at PDP/cart, not only at the checkout page.
- **Global-e pricing via SFCC price books (REG-041, Confirmed 05-05):** SFCC holds all price books including for Global-e markets. AP21 feeds base RRP pricebooks per currency (AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) and fixed pricelists per Global-e market to SFCC via MuleSoft. A nightly job generates Global-e-derived pricebooks using FX rates and coefficients from Global-e. Global-e handles shipping charges, duties, and taxes at checkout. SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency to Global-e. SFCC does **not** independently calculate shipping, duties, or tax for Global-e paths. (REG-040 was retired 05-05 — superseded by REG-041.)

_For checkout-specific frontend behaviour (redirect trigger, data flow), see [checkout.md](checkout.md)._

---

## 4. Currency & Tax (REG-036 – REG-042)

- Single currency per domestic storefront: AUD, USD, GBP, EUR (REG-039). No multi-currency toggle. (Open: Zimmermann would like multi-currency on AU domestic to offer NZD — not yet agreed.)
- Tax display: AU (GST), UK (VAT) via SFCC native tax tables, EU domestic (VAT) via Avalara (REG-037). The EU domestic site supports one RRP but must support multiple EU zone VAT requirements in the order payload. US domestic: prices excl. tax; Avalara calculates sales tax at checkout (REG-038). NZ and New Caledonia on AU: Avalara (REG-037).
- Sale pricing: was/now format. If price changes again after sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042).
- Prices shown in storefront currency on PDP, PLP, mini-cart, cart (REG-036).

---

## 5. EU Locale Billing Fields (REG-011)

The system will display locale-specific additional billing fields where required (e.g. Italian Codice Fiscale or VAT ID). **Open (REG-011):** confirm with Egaltine which other locales (e.g. Spanish NIF, French SIRET) require additional fields. Do not implement until confirmed.

---

## 6. Language & Translation (REG-044 – REG-047)

- EU domestic supports 4 languages: EN, FR, IT, ES (REG-044). All other storefronts English only.
- All customer-facing content (CMS from Contentful, product data from Product API) translated across EU locale variants (REG-045). CMS must accommodate translation-driven adjustments (e.g. button resize for translated CTAs).
- English is the site-wide fallback where translated content is unavailable (REG-046).
- Translation pipeline (REG-047, de-scoped 2026-05-25): the end-to-end configurable pipeline requirement was withdrawn. Translation occurs directly between **Contentful and Transperfect** outside the PWA Kit's concern; any SFCC-held strings (e.g. system messages, validation copy) are translated via static JSON files. No FE work required beyond consuming the translated Contentful payloads.

---

## 7. Consent (Didomi) (REG-048 – REG-056)

- Cookie consent banner shown on first visit on all storefronts, managed by Didomi CMP (REG-048). Consent preferences persist across sessions (REG-050).
- **Do not load any third-party tracking or marketing script until Didomi consent is granted** (REG-049).
- Consent categories: Performance, Analytics, Marketing — Required is non-configurable (REG-051). Subject to legal confirmation but expected to follow existing Didomi process.
- Customers can review and update preferences at any time via the storefront (REG-052). Granular consent allowed — individual categories can be toggled independently (REG-053).

### Per-storefront defaults (REG-054)

| Storefront                   | Default                                          |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| EU storefronts               | Opted-out (no action = opted-out)                |
| US domestic                  | Explicit choice required (no action = opted-out) |
| AU, US international, HK, ME | Opted-in by default                              |

- GTM integrated with Didomi for **Google Consent Mode v2** signal passing across all storefronts (REG-055).
- Hashed email passed to GTM at order confirmation for Enhanced Conversions (REG-056).
- Didomi consent notice greys out all site content and prevents interaction until the consent flow completes (HPC-013/014).

---

## 8. Marketing Opt-In (REG-057 – REG-059)

- Marketing opt-in checkbox displayed at two points: guest checkout entry page and account registration page. Unchecked by default on all storefronts **except US (pre-checked)** (REG-057).
- Opt-in state sync: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys. Passed to Omneo on order placement for guests, on account registration for registered customers (REG-058).
- Registered customers can update marketing preferences in My Account → synced to Omneo (REG-059).

_Open: guest checkout journey & marketing opt-in touchpoints (REG-057, REG-058) — see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies"._

---

## 9. Inside Chat (HPC-039 – HPC-040)

- Customer support chat widget shown on relevant pages per Inside Chat's own display rules.
- Must only be initialised **after Didomi consent** for the relevant category.

---

## 10. GDPR & Privacy (REG-060 – REG-067)

- Right-to-erasure: deletion of customer PII from SFCC including registered accounts, saved addresses, and guest order data (REG-060).
- DSAR and erasure requests managed via the SFCC GDPR cartridge, replacing the current manual legal/IT ticketing process (REG-061).
- Configurable data retention per market in SFCC BM; auto-purge on expiry (REG-062).
- Adyen payment tokens held in SFCC are deleted as part of right-to-erasure (REG-063).
- Localised privacy policy per storefront (REG-064).
- DSAR export of all PII held in SFCC in a portable, readable format (REG-065).
- Consent audit log capturing when and how consent was captured (REG-066).
- Breach notification reporting filterable by country and US state (REG-067).

---

## 11. Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL

This content now lives in its own PRD: [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md), covering Magento→SFCC data migration (DMU-001 – DMU-012), URL strategy and redirects (DMU-013 – DMU-020), SEO (DMU-021 – DMU-041), and GEO routing foundations (DMU-042). Storefront routing, consent, and currency remain in this file.

---

## 12. Open Items

See **AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies"** for the full list. Regional open items (data migration / URL / SEO / GEO open items live in [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md)):

- EU locale-specific billing fields (Italian Codice Fiscale, Spanish NIF, French SIRET) — confirmation with Egaltine pending (REG-011)
- Global-e + Didomi consent interaction — TBD
- Guest checkout journey & marketing opt-in touchpoints (REG-057, REG-058)
- Multi-currency on AU domestic to offer NZD — added to enhancement log, **not in go-live scope** (REG-039)

**Resolved since previous version:**

- US single-vs-separate site (REG-005) — **Updated 2026-07-10** to two separate SFCC sites (US domestic `/us/` via SFCC; US international `/en-ca/` via Global-e). The 2026-06-11 single-site decision has been superseded. New site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` pending BM confirmation.
- Denmark routing — confirmed → EU Domestic via Country to Storefront Mapping sheet
- REG-047 translation pipeline — de-scoped (Contentful↔Transperfect direct; SFCC strings via JSON)

########## SFCC-801 context in drawer-tabs-plan ##########
- **SFCC-736 "pdp/drawer"** (assigned to Tim, Squad-A, In Progress) — the drawer _shell_ only:
  slide-in panel, backdrop overlay, close button, tab navigation header. Accepts tab content as
  children. Does not own tab content.
- **SFCC-195 "PDP – Slide Out - Details & Care"** — first tab's content (Details & Care),
  triggered by info links on PDP. Depends on SFCC-736's shell/tab API.

Known future consumers of the same Drawer/Tabs primitives (NOT in scope now, but the API must
stay generic enough for them): SFCC-102 (Size & Fit tab), SFCC-266 (EU Environmental Qualities
tab), SFCC-267 (Shipping & Returns + Assistance tabs), SFCC-101 (Measmerize/Find My Size CTA),
SFCC-742 (Wishlist login panel — renders as children inside pdp/drawer), SFCC-801 (global
country/currency selector — separate right-anchored drawer, same shape), **SFCC-297 (Find in
Boutique — confirmed by Tim to use this same Drawer)**. A story also exists for the Add to Cart /
View Cart mini-cart (not yet shared/ticketed here) — confirmed by Tim it will invoke this Drawer
to display the mini-cart once picked up, consistent with `cart.md` PRD's "opens as an overlay on
Add to Bag CTA or bag icon click."

## Research findings

- **No existing Tabs component anywhere** — not in `overrides/`, not in the base
  `@salesforce/retail-react-app` template (confirmed via full grep, zero `Tabs`/`TabList` usage

New site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` pending BM confirmation.
111:- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Here is the evidence-backed report. --- # SFCC-801 sizing research — findings ## 1. `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` **Absolute path:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/config/countries.ts` (129 lines) **The single most important finding for sizing: this file does NOT model a shopper-facing country list. It models the 11 storefront routes.** It is a routing/config table keyed by URL slug, not a catalogue of countries a shopper can pick. The type: ```ts export type CountryConfig = { /** URL path segment, e.g. 'au', 'us', 'fr-eu' */ urlSlug: string; /** The real SFCC site this locale routes to */ sfccSiteId: string; /** IETF locale used by PWA Kit / SFCC, e.g. 'en-AU' */ locale: string; /** ISO 4217 currency code */ currency: string; /** ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 shipping/tax country */ shippingCountry: string; checkoutOwner: CheckoutOwner; // 'sfcc' | 'global-e' | 'hybrid' globalEPricing: boolean; /** Key used to filter boutique locations for this region */ boutiqueRegion: string; }; ``` It is assembled from two halves — a generated half and a hand overlay: ```ts const COUNTRY_OVERLAY: Record = { au: { shippingCountry: 'AU', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'australia' }, us: { shippingCountry: 'US', checkoutOwner: 'hybrid', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' }, 'en-ca': { shippingCountry: 'CA', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' }, // TBC — pending ZimmermannUSIntl uk: { shippingCountry: 'GB', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'uk' }, 'en-eu': { shippingCountry: 'DE', ... boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout ... hk: { shippingCountry: 'HK', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'hong-kong' }, 'en-ae': { shippingCountry: 'AE', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'middle-east' }, }; ``` **Total count: 11 entries.** (`COUNTRY_OVERLAY` has 11 keys; `GENERATED_COUNTRIES` in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts` has the same 11; the `.filter(([slug]) => slug in GENERATED_COUNTRIES)` therefore drops nothing.) Per-field answer to your question: - **Currency? Yes** — from `countries.generated.ts` (`currency: 'AUD'` etc.). - **Locale? Yes** — same source. - **Region? Only obliquely.** There is `boutiqueRegion` (`'australia' | 'usa' | 'uk' | 'europe' | 'hong-kong' | 'middle-east'`), but its documented purpose is `/** Key used to filter boutique locations for this region */` — store-locator filtering, not selector grouping. It has 6 values and does **not** match REG-021's required grouping (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas). - **Flag? No.** No flag field exists. **Two defects worth carrying into refinement:** **(a) A stale comment.** Lines 69–74 claim `en-ca` is excluded: > `'en-ca' (US international) is defined here ready to go, but has no matching entry in countries.generated.ts yet — it's excluded from the final COUNTRIES export below until the ZimmermannUSIntl site is added to config/sites.overlay.js` That is no longer true — `countries.generated.ts` (synced `2026-08-07`) contains `'en-ca': { sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannUSIntl', locale: 'en-CA', currency: 'USD' }`, and `sites.overlay.js` has the site. `en-ca` **is** in the export. Matches your memory note that US-INTL merged and is live. **(b) A live currency conflict between config and the PRD, directly material to a selector that renders a currency code per row:** | Slug | `countries.generated.ts` | `regional.md` PRD table | |---|---|---| | `hk` | `currency: 'USD'` | **HKD** (SFCC price books) | | `en-ae` | `currency: 'EUR'` | **AED** (SFCC price books) | `config/sites.generated.js` agrees with the generated file (`ZimmermannHK: supportedCurrencies: ['USD']`, `ZimmermannME: ['EUR']`). So BM and the PRD genuinely disagree. SFCC-801 cannot render a trustworthy currency column until this is resolved. **Unresolved block already declared in the file header:** ``` * Unresolved — do not hard-code: * - NZ/Oceania currency routing * - Denmark routing * - China ``` (Note `regional.md` §1 says Denmark **is** resolved → EU Domestic, so this header is also partly stale.) --- ## 2. `config/sites.js` **Path:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/sites.js` — 56 lines, and it contains **no data**. It is a merge function only: ```js const generated = require('./sites.generated'); const overlay = require('./sites.overlay'); module.exports = overlay.map(({ id, sfccSiteId, locales }) => { ... }); ``` Real data lives in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/sites.overlay.js` (hand-maintained routing) and `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/sites.generated.js` (SCAPI-synced l10n, last synced `2026-08-07T07:53:08.246Z`). **10 PWA sites backed by 8 SFCC sites.** The EU-domestic split is the reason for the mismatch — four PWA sites share one real SFCC site: | PWA site `id` | `sfccSiteId` | URL prefix (alias) | supportedLocales (PWA) | defaultLocale | supportedCurrencies | defaultCurrency | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `ZimmermannAU` | — | `/` (root, no alias) | `en` | `en` | `['AUD']` | AUD | | `ZimmermannUS` | — | `/us/` | `en-US` | `en-US` | `['USD']` | USD | | `ZimmermannUSIntl` | — | `/en-ca/` | `en-CA` | `en-CA` | `['USD']` | USD | | `ZimmermannUK` | — | `/uk/` | `en-GB` | `en-GB` | `['GBP']` | GBP | | `ZimmermannEUen` | `ZimmermannEU` | `/en-eu/` | `en-GB` | `en-GB` | `['EUR']` | EUR | | `ZimmermannEUfr` | `ZimmermannEU` | `/fr-eu/` | `fr` | `fr` | `['EUR']` | EUR | | `ZimmermannEUit` | `ZimmermannEU` | `/it-eu/` | `it` | `it` | `['EUR']` | EUR | | `ZimmermannEUes` | `ZimmermannEU` | `/es-eu/` | `es` | `es` | `['EUR']` | EUR | | `ZimmermannEUIntl` | — | `/en-ch/` | `en-CH` | `en-CH` | `['EUR']` | EUR | | `ZimmermannHK` | — | `/hk/` | `en-HK` | `en-HK` | `['USD']` | USD | | `ZimmermannME` | — | `/en-ae/` | `en-AE` | `en-AE` | `['EUR']` | EUR | **Critical for a currency selector: every site has exactly ONE supported currency.** There is no multi-currency site anywhere. This is corroborated by `regional.md` REG-039: *"Single currency per domestic storefront: AUD, USD, GBP, EUR (REG-039). **No multi-currency toggle.**"* So SFCC-801's "currency" is a **display consequence of picking a country**, never an independent control. Also note `sites.js`'s deliberate refusal to use SCAPI's own default locale: ```js // NOT source.defaultLocale — that's SCAPI's site-level default for the // real SFCC site, which can be a locale this PWA site doesn't even // support ... Every PWA site has exactly one locale in its overlay, so // that locale IS its default, full stop. defaultLocale: locales[0].id, ``` **`config/default.js` URL config** (`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/default.js`): ```js url: { site: 'path', locale: 'path', showDefaults: false, showBasePath: false, ... }, defaultSite: 'ZimmermannAU', // AU has no alias — it is the defaultSite and showDefaults: false keeps it at the root (/). siteAliases: { ZimmermannUK: 'uk', ZimmermannUS: 'us', ZimmermannUSIntl: 'en-ca', ZimmermannEUen: 'en-eu', ZimmermannEUfr: 'fr-eu', ZimmermannEUit: 'it-eu', ZimmermannEUes: 'es-eu', ZimmermannEUIntl: 'en-ch', ZimmermannHK: 'hk', ZimmermannME: 'en-ae', }, ``` `config/default.js` is **Tier 1 / absolute** per AGENTS.md Hard Rule #4 — the verified-session exception does not apply. SFCC-801 must not need to touch it. --- ## 3. `.docs/prd/regional.md` **Path:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/prd/regional.md` (189 lines, *"Last updated: 2026-06-19"*). **Storefronts/locales:** *"**8 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions in Business Manager:** AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME. A MX domestic site is planned for 2027."* and *"11 active locales across the 8 sites (REG-043)."* ### The selector passages, verbatim (§2, REG-020 – REG-028) > - **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU (REG-020, REG-025). Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field (REG-021). Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, all other storefronts English only (REG-023). Selected EU locale reflected in URL (REG-024). > - AU is gated and does **not** allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites (REG-025). > - **China** selected from any country selector routes to HK (REG-026). > - **Australia** selected from another storefront's country selector (i.e. clients outside Oceania) routes to HK (REG-027). > - Global-e checkout locks the shipping country — determined by country selector pre-checkout, cannot be changed inside Global-e (REG-028). And the mismatch slide-out that feeds it (REG-014 – REG-019): > All other storefronts use **mismatch detection** (REG-014): a country slide-out is shown on the first visit if the user's IP country does not match the storefront's shipping region (REG-015). Two CTAs: redirect to the appropriate storefront, or **open the country selector** (REG-016). A warning is shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-017). **Four sizing consequences from these quotes:** 1. **REG-021 names three region groups** — *Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas* — which is **not** the 6-value `boutiqueRegion` field in `countries.ts`. The grouping has no data source. Africa also has no home in that three-group list despite `/en-ch/` owning all of Africa per §1. 2. **REG-021 mandates a search field**, which your prompt's description omits. That is extra scope. 3. **REG-023 folds language into the same selector** — so "optionally language" is actually *required*, and EU-domestic is the only multi-language case. 4. **REG-026/REG-027 are routing traps:** picking China routes to HK, and picking Australia from a non-Oceania storefront routes to **HK, not AU**. A naive `country → site` map gets both wrong. **AU gating (REG-009, REG-025):** > **AU is gated** to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IPs only (REG-009). AU is the `x-default` hreflang and must remain crawlable, so it is never blocked at the network level. A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect... Combined with REG-020's *"available on all storefronts except AU"* — **the selector must not render on the AU storefront at all.** AU is the default dev site (`defaultSite: 'ZimmermannAU'`, root `/`), so the component's default local-dev context is the one storefront where it is forbidden. That is a real Storybook/QA friction point. **EU-domestic language choice (§6, REG-044–047 + §2 REG-029–035):** EU domestic supports EN/FR/IT/ES; all other storefronts English only. Country→language mapping (REG-030) is France/Monaco→FR, Italy/San Marino→IT, Spain→ES, everything else→`/en-eu/` (REG-034). **The ~200-country routing table exists only in the source spreadsheet, not in the repo.** §1 states: *"The full per-country mapping lives in the source sheet; the FE only needs the routing logic"* — then lists destination countries per storefront in prose. There is also this warning: > Geographic anomalies (mapping sheet): Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname all route to **EU International** despite being in the Americas/African geography. This follows fulfilment territory, not landmass — flagged for awareness; **routing tables must follow the sheet verbatim.** So the country list SFCC-801 needs must be **transcribed from `Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx` ("Country to Storefront Mapping" sheet)** and cannot be derived from anything in the repo. --- ## 4. Memory docs — `sprintScope.md` / `projectState.md` **Direct answer: neither file mentions SFCC-801, SFCC-688, SFCC-817, SFCC-49, SFCC-823, "country selector", "region selector", "locale selector", or "geolocation". A case-insensitive grep for all of those terms returned zero matches in both files.** **Both are stale, and materially so:** - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` — 126 lines, mtime `Jul 9 2026`, self-labelled *"Draft (2026-06-23). To be refined as sprints are confirmed."* Its "Current position" reads **"Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress)"** and its sprint calendar ends at *"Sprint 6 — 7 Sep – 11 Sep"*. Today is 2026-09-22. It also never lists a regional/selector workstream after "Regional Storefront (Part 2)" in Sprint 2. This contradicts your own memory note (`project_real_sprint_cadence.md`: Jira ground truth has Sprint 3 = 11–24 Aug, Sprint 5 ending 21 Sep). **Do not use sprintScope.md to place SFCC-801.** - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/memory/projectState.md` — 169 lines, mtime `Aug 28 2026`, header *"Last updated: 2026-08-24 (SFCC-55 global footer...)"*. ~4 weeks stale; it predates all the SFCC-831/689 country-language work that is actually on disk. The closest `projectState.md` gets is a pending-work line: > Full multi-site routing — 8 SFCC sites across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME). **US site topology updated (REG-005, 2026-07-10):** US splits into two separate SFCC sites... **Where the real current state actually lives:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/session-notes.md`, `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/registry/components.md`, and `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/temp/SFCC-736-195-drawer-tabs-plan.md`. That last file is the only place in the repo that names SFCC-801: > Known future consumers of the same Drawer/Tabs primitives (NOT in scope now, but the API must stay generic enough for them): ... SFCC-742 (Wishlist login panel...), **SFCC-801 (global country/currency selector — separate right-anchored drawer, same shape)**, SFCC-297... and: > Header content is a plain slot (children) — ZimmDrawer itself knows nothing about tabs, so **SFCC-801/742's simple-title-header use case** and SFCC-736's tabbed use case both compose on top of it. **So SFCC-801's drawer shell was explicitly designed for and is already built.** --- ## 5. Other country-list data sources, and flag assets ### There IS a second country list — and it is not usable as-is `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/constants/index.ts` line 132, `SHIPPING_COUNTRY_CODES`: ```ts export const SHIPPING_COUNTRY_CODES = [ {value: 'AU', label: 'Australia'}, {value: 'AT', label: 'Austria'}, ... {value: 'HK', label: 'Hong Kong SAR China'}, ... {value: 'US', label: 'United States'}, ] ``` **33 entries, `{value,label}` only — no currency, no region, no flag.** Its sole consumer is the checkout address form: `overrides/app/components/forms/useAddressFields.tsx:9` imports it and feeds it to a `
